wood.definition: A hard material from trees used for building and making objects.

stone.definition: Building material consisting of a piece of rock hewn in a definite shape for a special purpose.

granite.definition: Something having the quality of granite (unyielding firmness).

clay.definition: A soft material shaped by hand to make objects.

sand.definition: Small loose grains of rock or mineral material.

bamboo.definition: The hard woody stems of bamboo plants.

cork.definition: Outer bark of the cork oak.

slate.definition: (formerly) a writing tablet made of slate.

limestone.definition: A sedimentary rock consisting mainly of calcium that was deposited by the remains of marine animals.
limestone.exampleUsage: The limestone was identified during the lesson.

steel.definition: A strong metal used to build and support structures.

aluminum.definition: A silvery ductile metallic element found primarily in bauxite.

silver.definition: Having the white lustrous sheen of silver.

bronze.definition: An alloy of copper and tin and sometimes other elements.

brass.definition: An alloy of copper and zinc.

titanium.definition: A light strong grey lustrous corrosion-resistant metallic element used in strong lightweight alloys (as for airplane parts).

cotton.definition: Soft silky fibers from cotton plants in their raw state.

silk.definition: A fabric made from the fine threads produced by certain insect larvae.
silk.exampleUsage: The silk was identified during the lesson.

wool.definition: Soft hair from sheep, used to make warm cloth.

linen.definition: A high-quality paper made of linen fibers or with a linen finish.

denim.definition: (used in the plural) close-fitting trousers of heavy denim for manual work or casual wear.

velvet.definition: Resembling velvet in having a smooth soft surface.

satin.definition: A smooth fabric of silk or rayon.

cashmere.definition: A soft fabric made from the wool of the Cashmere goat.

plastic.definition: Capable of being molded or modeled (especially of earth or clay or other soft material).

rubber.definition: Any of various synthetic elastic materials whose properties resemble natural rubber.

fiberglass.definition: A covering material made of glass fibers in resins.

carbon-fiber.definition: A lightweight material made from extremely thin carbon strands arranged in a highly ordered structure. It is usually added to plastics and other materials to make composite parts stronger and stiffer.

vinyl.definition: Shiny and tough and flexible plastic.

silicone.definition: Any of a large class of siloxanes that are unusually stable over a wide range of temperatures.

foam.definition: A mass of small bubbles formed in or on a liquid.

resin.definition: Any of a class of solid or semisolid viscous substances obtained either as exudations from certain plants or prepared by polymerization of simple molecules.

concrete.definition: A hard building material used for paths and surfaces.

brick.definition: A small rectangular block used to build walls.

cement.definition: A hard building material made by mixing cement, sand, and water.

plaster.definition: A white material that becomes hard and is used for casting shapes.

drywall.definition: A board material used to make the inside walls of a building.

insulation.definition: The state of being isolated or detached.

tile.definition: A flat thin rectangular slab (as of fired clay or rubber or linoleum) used to cover surfaces.

grout.definition: A thin mortar that can be poured and used to fill cracks in masonry or brickwork.

lumber.definition: The wood of trees cut and prepared for use as building material.
